outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The agent applied an extra filter “Learning Product: Courses” even though the task already says “filter courses”; this doesn’t harm the outcome. (2) The agent included review counts and called them an “enrollment proxy,” but it did not actually convert reviews into enrollment counts and correctly marked enrollment as unavailable; this is mostly wording/labeling.

Critical issues: The key failure is that the agent did not actually report the three highest-rated matching courses. DOM evidence (e.g., states 6, 11, 18) shows multiple filter-matching courses with rating 4.8 (e.g., “Prepare Data for Exploration” ★4.8 (23K), “Prompt Engineering for ChatGPT” ★4.8 (8.1K), and others). Despite that, the agent’s reported top three included “Introduction to Statistics” rated 4.6, which cannot be part of the top-three-by-rating when several higher-rated (4.8) matching courses are visible. The agent also did not apply any “Highest Rated” sort (the sort control only shows Best Match/Newest), so selecting the first three in “Best Match” order does not satisfy the explicit “highest-rated” ranking requirement.

What the agent did accomplish: It successfully reached Coursera’s Data Science browse page without signing in, applied the requested filters (English, Beginner, 1–3 months; and effectively Data Science via the browse context; plus Courses), and it correctly avoided guessing enrollment counts (reported as unavailable, consistent with DOM showing only review counts). However, because the primary deliverable is the correct highest-rated trio, and the agent’s final list is demonstrably not the three highest-rated matching courses, the task is not successfully completed from an average user perspective.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted Coursera course results constrained to Data Science subject, Beginner level, English language, and 1–3 months duration, then to be told which three matching courses have the highest displayed ratings (with title, rating, and enrollment count if Coursera shows it). A reasonable user would be flexible about minor formatting and whether “Data Science” is satisfied via the Data Science browse context vs. a subject facet, but would not be flexible on the “three highest-rated” requirement or on making up enrollment counts.
